newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG CLAIMS FOURTH SEASON VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG CLAIMS FOURTH SEASON VICTORY.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg continued her domination of the women's World Cup circuit on Sunday by recording her fourth victory of the season in a super-giant slalom.

Wiberg posted a fastest time of one minute 39.98 seconds on the hard and icy 2,000-metre long Strohsack piste in sunny weather at this Austrian resort. Italian world super-G champion Isolde Kostner was second in 1:40.26.
The 26-year-old Swede increased her leading total in the overall standings to 863 points with her second super-G win of the winter after a victory in Lake Louise, Canada, in November.
She also won slaloms in Semmering, Austria, and Maribor, Slovenia.
Wiberg's fiercest rival in the overall race, titleholder Katja Seizinger of Germany, was third in 1:40.34 and remains second in the standings on 649 points.
Italian Barbara Merlin had a nasty fall on the final jump when she lost control of her skis, but walked away uninjured.
